title: Git on iPhone and iPad | Acode
description: Manage Git repositories on iPhone and iPad with Acode’s terminal and editor. Review changes, create commits, and connect to your Git host.
heroHeadline: Edit and version your projects on iOS
heroSubheadline: Use Git in Acode’s Alpine Linux terminal for small repository workflows, from reviewing a diff to preparing a commit.
problemPoints: Manage Git repositories on iPhone and iPad with Acode’s terminal and editor. Review changes, create commits, and connect to your Git host.
solutionPoints: Acode for iPhone and iPad is currently marked Coming soon on the website. Check the home page for release availability.

features.title: Review before committing
features.description: Use git status and git diff to inspect changes before staging files.

features.title: Keep code and history together
features.description: Work from a repository in the terminal’s filesystem and open its files in Acode to edit them.

features.title: Connect to your Git host
features.description: Fetching and pushing require a network connection and authentication accepted by your Git host. Keep credentials private and out of project files.

setupSteps.title: Install Git
setupSteps.description: In the terminal, run apk update && apk add git.

setupSteps.title: Set your identity
setupSteps.description: Set git config --global user.name and git config --global user.email with the name and email you want on commits.

setupSteps.title: Open a repository
setupSteps.description: Clone a repository you have permission to access, or work with an existing local repository.

setupSteps.title: Review your edits
setupSteps.description: Run git status and git diff, then stage only the files you intend to commit.

faqs.question: Can I work offline?
faqs.answer: Local edits, status checks, diffs, and commits work without a network connection. Cloning, fetching, and pushing need access to the remote host.

faqs.question: Is performance the same as a desktop?
faqs.answer: The iOS terminal uses emulation. Large repositories and intensive operations may take longer; start with a small project.
